error: The headline claim says its population is all orders, while the spec and its own caveats say delivered orders.
warning_texts: audit/check_plan.json has no deterministic rule over a claim's population or period fields: caveats_declared only matches caveat text, so a claim whose population field contradicts its caveats (as CLM-NET-REVENUE does) passes gate_claims_machine unchallenged.

CLM-REFUND-RATE states its basis in the caveat through the identifier paying_customers rather than plain words; the meaning is clear and the topic rule accepts it, but the release should render it as paying customers so a reader does not see a column name.

The refund rate basis moves the figure materially on this data: paying customers give 27/57 = 0.473684, while the order-row reading would give 33/174 = 0.189655, so any surface that omits the basis invites a misread.

metrics/calculated_metrics.json describes net_revenue_pl, net_revenue_de and net_revenue_cz with the formula text 'SUM(net_amount) WHERE country = country', which is tautological; the values are correct but the formula does not say which country it filters.
analysis/answers/R01.json restates the question as net revenue for the reported quarter and drops the population qualifier (delivered orders inside the period) that raw_data/questions.md puts in R01.
summary: All five claim values recompute exactly from raw_data/orders.csv (net 35741.52, refund rate 27/57 = 0.473684, PL 11181.67, DE 11032.61, CZ 13527.24) and the machine recalc is rooted in raw only, but CLM-NET-REVENUE declares its population as all orders inside the period while its value is computed on delivered orders inside the period (174 rows); taken literally that label selects 200 rows and a net of 41881.34, so the claim is mislabelled and contradicts its own caveat.
